articles.title: Markets likely to move beyond geopolitics, focus to shift to earnings: Devina Mehra
articles.content: Devina Mehra believes geopolitical deals like a potential Iran-US agreement won't drive Indian equities, with earnings and liquidity being key. Mehra also highlights the dangers of emotional investing and emphasizes the importance of global diversification beyond the US.

articles.title: UPDATE 1-UK bond yields fall to two-month low on US-Iran preliminary deal
articles.content: British government bond yields dropped to a two-month low on Monday. This followed a preliminary peace deal between the United States and Iran. Oil prices fell more than five percent. Two-year gilt yields dropped over eight basis points. Ten-year yields also fell. This eased fears of a wider stagflationary shock. Investors became dovish on future rates outlook.

articles.title: Nilesh Shah bats for minimum qualifying criteria for F&O trading after Maharashtra man kills family, self over Rs 1.8 cr loss
articles.content: Following a tragic incident in Maharashtra linked to stock market losses, Kotak AMC's Nilesh Shah called for mandatory qualification criteria for derivatives trading. Citing rising retail F&O losses and SEBI data showing most traders lose money, he urged stronger safeguards to curb excessive speculation in the market.

articles.title: Rajesh Exports shares jump 5% after 30% crash in 7 days. How the alleged Rs 15.15 lakh cr fraud saga unfolded

articles.title: Maruti Suzuki shares jump over 4%. How is the new E100 regulation triggering a surge?
articles.content: Maruti Suzuki shares surged after the government approved legal recognition for 100% ethanol blend fuel (E100). This move, championed by Nitin Gadkari, aims to reduce India's import dependence and boost energy security. Maruti's recent launch of India's first flex-fuel passenger vehicle positions it as a direct beneficiary of this policy shift.

articles.title: Rupee may gain ground as crude prices ease and FCNR inflows rise, says Navneet Damani
articles.content: The Indian rupee is poised for appreciation, driven by a significant drop in crude oil prices and anticipated substantial inflows from NRI FCNR(B) deposits. Recent tax reforms are expected to attract between $50 billion and $70 billion, potentially reversing the currency's recent depreciation and pushing it towards 92-93 levels.

articles.title: Supply recovery, not demand, will be oil market's key test: Vandana Hari
articles.content: Global crude oil prices have fallen significantly from wartime highs, but market expert Vandana Hari cautions against declaring victory. She anticipates a holding pattern until a formal memorandum of understanding is signed, with a gradual reopening of key energy routes expected to take months. Hari also believes demand destruction was temporary and expects it to return as prices stabilize.

articles.title: Middle East peace deal lifts market mood, but key challenges remain: William Lee
articles.content: Global markets are optimistic about a new peace framework involving Iran, easing energy supply and geopolitical concerns. Economic incentives and Israel's stance are critical factors influencing the outcome.

articles.title: Nifty Bank rallies 1,000 points; HDFC Bank, IndusInd, Yes Bank, and other stocks jump up to 3%. What lies ahead?
articles.content: Banking stocks rallied sharply on Monday, pushing the Nifty Bank index nearly 1,000 points higher as easing geopolitical tensions and falling oil prices boosted sentiment. articles.title: Vedanta listing: How billionaire Anil Agarwal's 'Fantastic 5' unlocked Rs 63,500 crore value with mega demerger
articles.content: Vedanta’s long-awaited demerger culminated with the listing of four newly spun-off businesses, triggering a sharp market re-rating and unlocking about Rs 63,500 crore in shareholder value. Since the demerger’s April 29 ex-date, investors have gained roughly 22.5%, with the combined market capitalization of the five standalone entities rising from Rs 3.02 lakh crore to Rs 3.66 lakh crore.

articles.title: Focus on structural trends, ignore market noise: Hiren Ved
